## Solution

**Setup.** The permutation is $\text{perm}[1..10]$ with $\text{perm}[1]=1$, $\text{perm}[10]=10$, and $\{\text{perm}[2],\ldots,\text{perm}[9]\}=\{2,\ldots,9\}$. We need exactly one local minimum among positions $2$–$9$.

**Sign sequence.** Define $s_i = \text{sgn}(\text{perm}[i+1]-\text{perm}[i])$ for $i=1,\ldots,9$. A local minimum at position $i$ corresponds to a "$-+$" transition at $(s_{i-1}, s_i)$.

**Boundary facts.** Since $\text{perm}[1]=1$ is the smallest, $s_1 = +$ always (position 2 is never a local min). Since $\text{perm}[10]=10$ is the largest, $s_9 = +$ always.

Since $s_1 = s_9 = +$, the number of "$-+$" transitions equals the number of "$+-$" transitions. Requiring **exactly one** local minimum means exactly one "$-+$" and one "$+-$" transition, so the sign pattern is:
$$\underbrace{+\cdots+}_{a}\;\underbrace{-\cdots-}_{b}\;\underbrace{+\cdots+}_{c}, \quad a+b+c=9,\; a,b,c\ge 1.$$

**Descent set.** The 8-element subsequence $(\text{perm}[2],\ldots,\text{perm}[9])$ has descent set exactly $D=\{a,\,a+1,\ldots,a+b-1\}$ (a contiguous block of $b$ descents), where $1\le a$, $b\ge 1$, $a+b\le 8$.

**Counting permutations with a contiguous descent set.** For descent set $D=\{a,\ldots,a+b-1\}$, the permutation has the shape:
$$\text{ascending} \;\prec\; \text{peak} \;\succ\; \text{descending} \;\succ\; \text{valley} \;\prec\; \text{ascending}$$
The peak is at position $a$, the valley at position $a+b$. Choosing valley value $v$ and peak value $p$ (with $v<p$), the $p-v-1$ middle elements split into: descending chain ($b-1$), left chain ($a-v$), right chain ($p-a-b$). This yields the multinomial count:

$$T(a,b) = \sum_{u=0}^{a-1}\sum_{w=0}^{8-a-b} \frac{(b+u+w-1)!}{(b-1)!\;u!\;w!}$$

**Verification of formula.** For $(a,b)=(1,1)$: descent set $\{1\}$, meaning $\text{perm}[2]>\text{perm}[3]$ and all else ascending. The valley must be $1$ (value $2$ in original), giving $T=7=\binom{8}{1}-1$. ✓  
For $(a,b)=(4,1)$: descent set $\{4\}$, count $= \binom{8}{4}-1=69$. ✓  
For $(a,b)=(1,7)$: fully decreasing, count $=1$. ✓

**Systematic computation** (using the closed form $T(a,b)=\sum_{u=0}^{a-1}\binom{u+b-1}{b-1}\binom{u+8-a}{u+b}$ derived via hockey-stick):

| $b$ | $T(a,b)$ for $a=1,2,\ldots$ | Sum |

**Total:**
$$247 + 522 + 501 + 268 + 83 + 14 + 1 = \boxed{1636}$$

**Setup.** The permutation is $\text{perm}[1..10]$ with $\text{perm}[1]=1$, $\text{perm}[10]=10$, and $\{\text{perm}[2],\ldots,\text{perm}[9]\}=\{2,\ldots,9\}$. We need exactly one local minimum among positions $2$–$9$.

**Sign sequence.** Define $s_i = \text{sgn}(\text{perm}[i+1]-\text{perm}[i])$ for $i=1,\ldots,9$. A local minimum at position $i$ corresponds to a "$-+$" transition at $(s_{i-1}, s_i)$.

**Boundary facts.** Since $\text{perm}[1]=1$ is the smallest, $s_1 = +$ always (position 2 is never a local min). Since $\text{perm}[10]=10$ is the largest, $s_9 = +$ always.

Since $s_1 = s_9 = +$, the number of "$-+$" transitions equals the number of "$+-$" transitions. Requiring **exactly one** local minimum means exactly one "$-+$" and one "$+-$" transition, so the sign pattern is:
$$\underbrace{+\cdots+}_{a}\;\underbrace{-\cdots-}_{b}\;\underbrace{+\cdots+}_{c}, \quad a+b+c=9,\; a,b,c\ge 1.$$

**Descent set.** The 8-element subsequence $(\text{perm}[2],\ldots,\text{perm}[9])$ has descent set exactly $D=\{a,\,a+1,\ldots,a+b-1\}$ (a contiguous block of $b$ descents), where $1\le a$, $b\ge 1$, $a+b\le 8$.

**Counting permutations with a contiguous descent set.** For descent set $D=\{a,\ldots,a+b-1\}$, the permutation has the shape:
$$\text{ascending} \;\prec\; \text{peak} \;\succ\; \text{descending} \;\succ\; \text{valley} \;\prec\; \text{ascending}$$
The peak is at position $a$, the valley at position $a+b$. Choosing valley value $v$ and peak value $p$ (with $v<p$), the $p-v-1$ middle elements split into: descending chain ($b-1$), left chain ($a-v$), right chain ($p-a-b$). This yields the multinomial count:

$$T(a,b) = \sum_{u=0}^{a-1}\sum_{w=0}^{8-a-b} \frac{(b+u+w-1)!}{(b-1)!\;u!\;w!}$$
